narr: A weak upper trough axis remained nearly stationary across East Texas, North Louisiana, and Southern Arkansas during the day on August 18th, with a weak surface trough stationary over these areas as well. These features focused the development of a cluster of showers and thunderstorms over portions of East Texas prior to and after daybreak, which moved very little throughout the morning. Given the very moist air mass in place and weak steering winds, these storms moved very little, with areas of locally heavy rainfall moving repeatedly over Central and Southern Smith County. Rainfall amounts of three to six inches fell across these areas, resulting in widespread flash flooding across the county. These storms eventually diminished during the mid and late morning hours.
ev: A water rescue was performed in the New Chapel Hill community at the intersection of County Road 289 and Highway 64 due to flash flooding.
Numerous roads were flooded in the city of Tyler.
Calloway Road was flooded, as well as the intersection of Highway 110 and Loop 323 in Tyler.
